title: Engineering Program Manager, Megapack Hardware, Enclosures
description:
**What to Expect**

Tesla’s Energy Engineering group is looking for a highly motivated individual to program-manage enclosure design engineering for Industrial Energy Products, including Megapack and Megapod. The enclosure is the structure the rest of the product is built into: body-in-white, doors, plinth and rack interfaces, thermal and electrical bays, and the joints to site and factory. It sits at the intersection of mechanical design, structural analysis, thermal, electrical, and harness packaging. If the enclosure is late, or the configuration is wrong, every downstream system is late.

This is a cross-functional role that requires coordination between many different groups within and outside of Tesla. You will interface with mechanical, CAE, thermal, electrical, and harness design engineering, system integration and validation, manufacturing engineering and operations, supply chain, compliance, reliability, safety, service, and field operations to define and drive enclosure development on new programs while also managing change on programs already in production or ramp.

As part of the Engineering Program Management team, you will be immersed in the design, validation, and manufacturing process and will shepherd enclosure scope from concept through prototype validation, production ramp, and sustaining change. You will use your engineering background to understand packaging and manufacturing constraints, structural and environmental risk, and what has to be released before the factory can build. You will communicate and present program status, highlight schedule risk, and develop recovery plans in the event of project slip.

As an Engineering Program Manager, you will be expected to operate with a high degree of autonomy on your programs while contributing to the tools, trackers, and cadence that improve risk and change management for the organization.
